title: How long is the second height of this triangle?
description: A triangle has a base of five units, a height of three units to it, and another side of four units. The area is found once, then written a second way with the other side as the base, and the two equal areas give the second height. Keeko doubts that the second height must also be three.
teaching_notes: One idea: one triangle has one area, so half of one base times its height equals half of another base times its height. Watch for students who think every height of a triangle has the same length.

source: In ΔABC, AX = 3 is the height to BC = 5, and AC = 4. Find th
video_script.why: The child sees that one triangle has one area, whichever side is taken as the base, so a known area and a second base give the second height.
video_script.substitution: the book's numbers: base BC = 5, height AX = 3, side AC = 4
video_script.anchor: the book's triangle ABC with the height AX to BC and the dotted height BY to AC
video_script.wrong_answer: the height to eigh C is also three
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes the height to AC as three, the same as AX. The two heights drop onto different sides, and the shorter side AC needs the longer height.
video_script.payoff_line: B Y is three point seven five units
maths_rules: BY = 3.75 is less than BC = 5, so the triangle can exist; AC = 4 is shorter than BC = 5, so BY = 3.75 is longer than AX = 3
video_script.design: One triangle all video. One area is written two ways, and the equal areas give the second height. Keeko's doubt: all heights are equal.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; triangle ABC with the base BC = 5 and the height AX = 3 drawn to it; the side AC = 4 marked; a dotted height BY from B to AC with a question mark

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.ax: the base BC = 5 and the height AX = 3 are marked
marks.ask: a dotted height BY from B to AC appears with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>Here is a triangle eigh B C.
<bookmark mark='ax'/>The side B C is five units, and the height eigh X down to it is three units.
<bookmark mark='side'/>The side eigh C is four units long.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How long is the height B Y, drawn from B down to the side eigh C?

beats.on_screen: the triangle holds still and the dotted height BY glows with its question mark

marks.stop: the dotted height BY glows in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: triangle ABC; the height AX drops to BC with a right angle mark; the height BY drops from B to AC; the rule area = 1/2 × base × height

marks.height: the height AX drops to BC with a right angle mark
marks.any: the height BY drops from B onto AC
marks.area: the rule area = 1/2 × base × height is written

narration: <bookmark mark='height'/>A height is the straight drop from a corner to the opposite side, at a right angle.
<bookmark mark='any'/>Any side can be the base, and each base has its own height.
<bookmark mark='area'/>The area of a triangle is half of the base times its height.

marks.given: the three given lengths are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the side B C is five units and the height eigh X is three units.
The side eigh C is four units.

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the height B Y, which drops onto the side eigh C.

marks.rule: the formula area = 1/2 × base × height is written with BC and AX
marks.calc: the numbers go in and 7.5 square units appears

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, find the area using the base B C and the height eigh X. The formula is half of base times height.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Half of five times three is seven point five square units.

marks.second: the same formula is written with the base AC and the height BY

narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Step two, write the same area again, with the base eigh C and the height B Y.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Half of four times B Y is two times B Y.

marks.same: the two area lines are joined by an equals sign

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step three, it is the same triangle, so the two areas must be equal.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>Two times B Y is seven point five.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Step four, divide both sides by two to get B Y alone.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Seven point five divided by two is three point seven five.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>B Y is three point seven five units.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the triangle
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: BY = 3, like AX; the bubble is struck out; AC is drawn shorter than BC and BY is shown longer than AX

marks.fix: the two heights glow on two different sides
marks.long: BY = 3.75 replaces the bubble beside the shorter side AC

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the height to eigh C is also three, the same as the height eigh X.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the two heights drop onto different sides, so they need not match.
<bookmark mark='long'/>The side eigh C is shorter than B C, so its height is longer.
It is three point seven five units.
